tools.description: Return a company's ledger masters, each with its opening balance as of the start of the books (`opening_balance`, `opening_balance_as_of`), on a freshly observed supported product and mode. fields=basic (the default) or fields=compliance, which adds paired party-master observations (GSTIN, PAN, MSME, bank, contact and address), each ledger's group `ancestry` and its `gst_duty_head`. GSTIN (compliance): `party_gstin` is the GSTIN in force on `party_gstin_as_of` (the optional `as_of`, YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD such as 20260331, else this computer's date; without fields=compliance, `as_of` is refused as ledger_masters_as_of_requires_compliance), taken from the ledger's dated registration history, or from the flat GSTIN field only when that history is empty or not returned (an empty flat field names no GSTIN). `party_gstin_status`: in_force, flat_field, no_gstin_in_force (a history with no GSTIN in force on that date; `party_gstin_registration_type` says whether that entry is registered), not_reported, or history_unreadable, which fails closed (an undated, misdated, malformed, repeated or contradictory history: party_gstin is null and the flat field unused). `party_gstin_flat` is always the flat field as read; `gstin_sources_disagree` is true when it names a GSTIN the in-force entry does not: both are reported, neither is chosen. For another date, such as a transaction's, pass it as `as_of` or read the dated `compliance.gst_registrations`. Duty head (compliance): `gst_duty_head` is `recognized` (`head`: cgst, igst, state_tax, sgst_utgst, ut_tax or cess; `raw`: the spelling Tally returned), `unrecognized` (raw kept), `not_tax_ledger`, `contradictory` or `absent`. `state_tax` (raw `State Tax`) and `sgst_utgst` (raw `SGST/UTGST`) are two spellings Tally has returned for a state-side head, kept apart: to sum state tax, include both. Ancestry (compliance): `chain` (nearest group first, each hop's `name` and `reserved_name`), `complete` (true only if resolved to the reserved account root) and `gap` (null when complete, else why it stopped: no_parent, group_absent, group_name_repeated, reserved_name_missing, cycle or exhausted). An incomplete chain is never padded or guessed: `chain` is exactly what was resolved, so check `complete` before treating it as exhaustive. A `reserved_name` starting with U+FFFD `#4;` is a Tally reserved value (written ``); `U+FFFD#4; Primary` is the account root, not a group a user named Primary. Group filter: `group` filters by group name. `group_scope` "immediate" (the default) matches only the ledger's own parent and does NOT include ledgers under sub-groups of `group`; "ancestry" matches anywhere in the resolved chain, the whole subtree (a ledger under `Bank OD A/c` matches `Loans (Liability)`), with either fields value, and a gap in a chain never counts as a match. A `group` filter reads the group collection (one more paired read with fields=basic) and returns `group_filter`: `excluded_subgroup_ledgers` (`count` left out for sitting under a sub-group of `group`, always 0 under ancestry scope, with `group_count` and up to 20 of those sub-groups in `groups`) and `unresolved_ancestry_ledgers` (ledgers not returned whose chain stops short of `group`, so whether they belong under it is unknown; counted over the whole book). GST details (compliance, opt-in): `include_gst_details` (a boolean, default false; with any other fields it is refused as ledger_masters_gst_details_requires_compliance) adds `compliance.gst_details` to each ledger: `observation` is `not_observed` (Tally returned no such list), `entries` (each dated entry with `applicable_from`, `taxability`, `source`, `ineligible_itc` and `states`; each state row has `state_name`, `slab_rates_present` and `rates` with `duty_head`, `valuation_type` and a `rate` whose `kind` is `absent`, `empty`, `zero` or `value` with `raw` as sent and `decimal`; `other_content_skipped` says content was not read) or `unreadable` (a `defect` for this ledger only). `absent`, `empty`, `zero` and `value` mean different things and are never merged. These are Tally's ledger-level details as sent: HSN/SAC and type of supply are not returned because no capture shows them, the place of supply is in the registration history, and slab rates are only flagged. `ineligible_itc` is `GSTINELIGIBLEITC` as sent (true Yes, false No, null absent): an ineligibility flag measured on one Purchase Accounts ledger only (PARTIAL), so never read true as eligible; a Yes elsewhere says nothing either way (see the result's `limitations`). The read is admitted at 8,000 bytes a ledger instead of 3,750, a margin over the one capture, not a measured ratio (the result's `limitations` has its sizes); a large book may be read in more parts or refused as too large. Large books (compliance): when the master-alteration mark (an upper bound on the ledgers, since every master raises it) puts the estimated response over budget, the ledgers are counted first, then read whole or, if the count does not fit, in parts by parent group; every counted ledger must come back exactly once, or the whole call is refused. Above a mark of 22,857 the count runs in AlterID-span slices of at most 4,000, one GUID-only request each; above 400,000 the call is refused before any ledger read (cause `ledger_catalogue_too_large`, with `size`), even for a company with fewer ledgers. Each refusal names its `cause`: `parent_over_budget`, `parent_partition_too_many_parts`, `parent_complement_over_budget`, `ledger_without_parent`, `parent_name_unsupported` (with `unsupported_parent_ledgers`), `parent_partition_duplicate_ledger_identity`, the `parent_part_*` coverage causes, `parent_part_response_too_large`, `ledger_span_slice_over_bound`, `ledger_span_duplicate_identity`, `ledger_span_census_empty`, `ledger_span_slice_malformed`, `ledger_span_identity_mismatch`, `ledger_span_slice_response_too_large` or `ledger_count_catalogue_too_large`. A size refusal refuses again on retry; fields=basic still reads the book. For `ledger_count_differs` (two counts, or a count and the ledgers read, disagree) or `ledger_count_company_differs` (Tally's own ledger count exceeds the census's), retry once while the book is quiet; for `ledger_count_company_invalid` (that count's answer was damaged) or `ledger_count_company_response_too_large`, retry once, then use fields=basic. A counted read reports `ledger_count_cross_check.status`: `matched`, `company_count_lower`, or `unavailable` (no count in Tally's answer, so no check ran). Currencies (compliance): a book with several Currency masters is read through the base Tally identifies: only plain base-currency ledgers are returned (`ledgers_scope` base_currency_ledgers_only); ledgers kept in another currency (`foreign_currency_ledgers_excluded`) and base-currency ledgers whose balances Tally shows in another currency (`base_currency_ledgers_mixed_excluded`) are named, never read. Paging: offset 0 always reads Tally afresh and holds the read; later pages are served from it while the book extent, ALTMSTID and ALTVCHID included, is unchanged, and each result reports `snapshot`. Pass the first page's `snapshot_id` on later pages to be refused as `listing_snapshot_changed` (cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`) rather than continue from a different read. With fields=compliance, repeat the first page's `as_of`: a snapshot serves only pages read as of the same date, so a later page without it (or across midnight) reads afresh, or is refused if it names the snapshot; the same holds for `include_gst_details`: a later page called without `include_gst_details` reads afresh and returns rows without `gst_details` (`snapshot.reused` false), and only a call that names snapshot_id is refused. A change that moves neither mark is not seen, so a later page can be up to 10 minutes old; every screen action measured so far moved one (a regroup, an opening change, a ledger create or delete, a voucher delete, a cancel, a save with no change; protocol reference section 11c.5, one run each). For what parties owe or are owed now, by their open bills, use outstandings instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: List a company's masters of one kind: voucher types with the numbering value Tally reports at the type level (see below: it is not their numbering method), active and optional flags and `series_numbering` (the numbering method, under Automatic its sub-method, and the duplicate setting of the type's series), godowns, units (with decimal places and whether simple), stock groups, stock items (with their own dated HSN and GST lists), cost centres (with their category), cost categories (with three allocation flags), or account groups (`groups`). Each row of another kind carries `name`, `guid`, `master_id`, `alter_id` and `parent` (null where it does not apply or is absent; a parent that is Tally's reserved root is written as U+FFFD `#4; Primary`, as in the group tree); a `groups` row carries `name`, `parent` and `reserved_name` only. Voucher types also carry `active`, `optional` (true, false or null when Tally did not say) and `numbering_method` (`automatic`, `manual`, `default`, `{"unrecognised": <raw text>}` for any other value Tally reports, or null when absent) and `series_numbering` (`{"observation":"observed","method":"automatic"|"manual"|"automatic_manual_override"|{"unrecognised": <raw text>},"duplicates":"prevented"|"not_prevented"}`, with `"sub_method":"auto_retain"|"auto_renumber"|"absent"|{"unrecognised": <raw text>}` under `automatic` and under no other method, `{"observation":"series_count","count":n}` when a type has no series or several, and nothing is read from it, or `{"observation":"field_invalid","code":...}`), read from a second paired read of the voucher-type export and joined to each row by GUID with the name as a second equality, so a type on one side only, or a GUID and name that disagree between the two reads, refuses the whole read (`masters_numbering_names_differ` for a type in one read only, `masters_numbering_identity_differs` for a GUID and name that disagree), as do `masters_numbering_collection_changed` (the numbering read changed between its two reads) and `masters_bound_premise_violated` (the numbering answer's row count or size), and a moved book is reported as `masters_extent_changed` in place of a join or premise refusal; units carry `decimal_places` and `simple`; cost centres carry `category` (always present: a centre without one is refused), cost categories `allocates_revenue`, `allocates_non_revenue` and `affects_stock`; stock items carry `hsn` and `gst` (see below); cost centres and categories are returned whether or not the company's Cost Centres setting is on (a book with the setting off was read with its centres, and a book with it on with its own), an empty cost-centre list does not say whether the feature is off or none is defined, and an empty cost-category list is refused (`masters_cost_categories_empty`, on the expectation that the predefined Primary Cost Category always exists), and how a voucher was allocated to a cost centre is not returned by this tool: the voucher reads carry it on each ledger entry (`cost_centre_allocations`). A stock item row carries `hsn` and `gst`, each the item's own dated list as Tally sent it: an `observation` of `entries` (sorted by `applicable_from`, each entry as sent; an HSN entry has `applicable_from`, `hsn_code` as text exactly as sent (never trimmed or cut), `description`, `source` and `other_content_skipped`; a GST entry has `applicable_from`, `taxability`, `source`, `ineligible_itc` (Tally's `GSTINELIGIBLEITC` as sent: true for Yes, false for No, null when the element was absent, never filled in; on one item it was Yes on the entry whose screen row read `Eligible for Input Tax Credit: No` and absent on the entry whose screen row read Yes, which fits an ineligibility flag; PARTIAL, one book, two rows, screen against wire; what an absent element means for the tax is not known, so do not read null as eligible or as ineligible, and do not read true as eligible; on an entry whose source is `As per Company/Stock Group` (the entry Tally adds itself on a first save; a person can also choose that source) a flag Tally sent is withheld: `ineligible_itc` is null and `ineligible_itc_withheld` is `tally_default_entry`, because the Yes seen on such an entry was never compared with the screen (both screen readings are of rows a person edited or keyed, and a row's origin and its flag cannot be told apart on one item); a flag Tally did not send stays null with no marker, and an entry with any other source is sent as it is), state rows and `other_content_skipped`, and a rate is `absent`, `empty`, `zero` or a `value` with its `raw` text and `decimal`, never merged), `unreadable` with its `defect` (an undated entry, an invalid date, a repeated field, two different entries on one date, a rate that is not a plain decimal, a credit flag other than Yes or No, a repeated state or duty-head row, or content only of a kind not modelled, such as text, a reference or CDATA directly in the list; that list of that item only, the read and the row stand) or `not_observed` (the row had no such list). Nothing chooses the code or the rate for a date. An empty list (`entries` with no entry) or `not_observed` is NOT a statement that the item has no HSN code or no GST rate: what its stock group or the company holds is not read. One thing was measured, on one book: after a code was keyed on a stock group, the group's four other items still carried empty lists; not measured: a GST rate on a group or on the company, an HSN code on the company, and whether an item that defers to a coded group inherits its code. ComplyEaze Bridge does not read that setting, so every stock item row carries `inherited_from_group_or_company: not_read`. Tally adds an entry of its own to an item when it is first saved (source `As per Company/Stock Group`, no code and no rate, dated the book's first day: 1 April 2025 on the one book measured, no other book's date measured, so recognise it by its source); it says the item defers to its group or the company. `state_name` and `valuation_type` carry the reserved-character marker (U+FFFD `#4;`) where Tally sends `Any` and `Not Applicable`. A Tally ERROR or LINEERROR anywhere in a list, markup inside a value, or a list cut off refuses the whole read. Measured on one synthetic book of TallyPrime 7.1 Silver (PARTIAL): a state row other than `Any`, slab rates, another release, a larger book and a zero-row stock-item answer are not measured. One kind per call, read inside one company, mode and book-extent bracket: the extent before and after must be equal and each collection is read twice and compared, so a book that changed during the read is refused. Whole reads only. Godowns, units, stock groups, stock items, cost centres and cost categories are read only when the book's master-alteration mark times an assumed worst-case row for that kind fits 16 MB (the mark counts the masters of every kind, so a book with few of this kind can be refused), and otherwise refuse before any request with `masters_too_large` and `size` (`master_alter_id`, `estimated_bytes`, `limit_bytes`, `limit_master_alter_id`); that admits marks up to 1,152 for godowns, 1,168 for units, 1,160 for stock groups, 489 for stock items (the item row is allowed for several dated entries: it is refused past 16,344 UTF-16 units, about seven further GST entries of the measured size, whatever its state rows; a limit of 489 refuses, by arithmetic, both client books measured, not tried on them), 1,037 for cost centres and 1,264 for cost categories. Retrying refuses again. The refusal's `size` carries `limit_master_alter_id`, the largest mark this kind is read at. Both stock-heavy client books measured, with marks of about 100,000 and 300,000, refuse godowns, units and stock groups, and by the same arithmetic stock items (cost centres, cost categories and stock items were not tried on them); how common such marks are across live books is unmeasured. `voucher_types` and `groups` have no size check before the read (voucher types keep the policy of ComplyEaze Bridge's other voucher-type read, and their second, numbering read is likewise sent with no size check). After a read of any kind other than `groups`, each row's length is checked against the assumed worst-case row (`masters_row_exceeds_bound`), and the row count, the rows' AlterIDs (at or under the mark, none repeated) and the response size (each collection is read twice, and the size check runs after both reads) are checked against the mark and the admitted size; a breach of those three refuses the whole read as `masters_bound_premise_violated` and returns no partial list, unless the closing extent shows the book moved, which is reported instead (`masters_extent_changed`). A response ComplyEaze Bridge cannot read refuses at once with a `masters_*` cause, and a `voucher_types` answer with no rows refuses as `masters_voucher_types_empty`, because every company has predefined voucher types. Not returned: alias names, counts and hints (no company NUM* fields), stock-item quantities, rates and values (use stock_summary), ledgers (use ledger_masters), and any write. The row shape was captured from one synthetic book on one licensed TallyPrime 7.1 (cost centres: three synthetic books, the third captured in a separate sitting whose own status read recorded TallyPrime 7.1, licence Silver, Education mode off; cost categories: two): the type-level numbering_method it carries is not the voucher type's numbering method: it read `None` for types a person had set to Automatic and to Manual on the screen, and the method is kept per number series, which `series_numbering` returns instead, so no value of numbering_method (`default`, `automatic`, `manual` or any other) says how a post is numbered. `series_numbering` was measured on one synthetic book (TallyPrime 7.1 Silver, Windows): 24 voucher types, each with one series named `Default`, of which three (Journal Automatic, Payment Manual with duplicates prevented, Receipt Manual with duplicates not prevented) were checked against Tally's screen; Automatic (Manual Override) through this tool (it is mapped from the series text measured on a synthetic book on 13 October 2026), more than one series, Multi-user Auto, a single series not named `Default`, a voucher type created new and other releases were not measured, an `unrecognised` method is never `manual`, and the integrated read, the two requests sent as one tool call, was run live on two synthetic books on 14 October 2026 and returned the numbering set or checked on Tally's screen for six types. `sub_method` is the series' own NUMBERINGSUBMETHOD (`auto_retain` is the screen's Retain Original Voucher No., `auto_renumber` its Renumber Vouchers, `absent` a series that printed none, and any other text, a blank one included, is returned raw under `unrecognised`); a Manual series printed Auto Retain too, which is not the numbering in force there, so it is not returned for one. It was measured on a second synthetic book (TallyPrime 7.1 Silver, Windows) and one voucher type, Receipt, set to Renumber Vouchers and back: with it on Renumber Vouchers, numbers already in the book changed, at the switch, when a voucher with an earlier date was entered by hand, and when one was sent by import without a number (the import's answer reported nothing altered and no voucher's AlterID moved); any other wording, a series that prints no sub-method, other voucher types, a batch of several vouchers, Gold, other releases and the same through ComplyEaze Bridge's own post are not measured. A value other than Automatic, Manual or Default is returned raw under `unrecognised`, not refused. `default` is Tally's reported value, not evidence that a type numbers automatically. The company's voucher-type count (NUMVOUCHERTYPES) did not equal the rows returned on two books (35 vs 26, 33 vs 24), and on one book equalled the number-series count (inferred to count series, unmeasured), so do not check these rows against it. The completeness of the voucher-type list is unverified: absence from it is not evidence that a voucher type is absent from the book. Under mask_parties, godown, stock-group, stock-item, cost-centre and cost-category names, their parents and a cost centre's category are masked, because a job-work godown, a supplier-named stock group or stock item or a customer-named cost centre can carry a party's name (Tally's reserved root as a parent is left as it is); a stock item's HSN codes and rates are not names and are returned as sent, but an HSN description, which Tally fills from its tariff list and a person can edit, is masked like an item name. Voucher-type, unit and account-group names are not masked: they are configuration labels, not counterparties. Education mode is refused. A first page (offset 0) always captures a fresh read and holds it in memory; a later page for the same kind (offset > 0) is served from it while the company's book extent, including ALTVCHID and ALTMSTID, is unchanged, at the cost of one small extent read. Each result reports `snapshot` (`id`, `master_alter_id`, `voucher_alter_id`, `read_at`, `reused`). Pass the first page's `snapshot_id` on later pages to have the call refused with `listing_snapshot_changed` (cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`) instead of continuing from a different read. A change that moves neither mark is not seen, so a later page can be up to 10 minutes old after such a change. tools.description: Answer what is outstanding: receivable and payable totals from Tally's own paired bills reports, ageing, the top parties and the open bills, on a freshly observed supported product and mode and a date valid for the operation. `as_of` is optional: left out, it is this computer's date (`tally_status` `today`), and the date used is always returned as `result.as_of`, whatever the state. `open_bills_total` counts every open bill in the requested direction, all of which `totals` and the ageing cover, and `open_bills_shown` counts the bills on this page (`limit` is not lowered when the response size shortens the page): when shown is less than total, say so plainly, for example "showing 500 of 1,240 open bills; the totals and the ageing cover all 1,240" (on a later page, the bills from offset + 1; on a partial read, both counts and the sentence cover the base-currency ledgers only, so say so in it), and ask for the next bills with `offset` set to `next_offset`. `receivable` and `payable` follow the sign of each bill's balance, as Tally's own Bills Receivable and Bills Payable reports scope them, not the type of party: a customer's advance or a credit note raised to a customer appears under payable, and a supplier's advance or a debit note raised to a supplier under receivable, because those reports carry no bill type. That holds for an advance or a note kept as its own bill: an on-account advance goes to the unallocated figure instead, and a credit note set against an open invoice reduces that invoice. Measured on one synthetic book (TallyPrime Silver 7.1). Read a bill's `kind` as a direction, not as owed by a customer or owed to a supplier. An unallocated amount's direction is the sign of the party's net unallocated balance, so an on-account receipt and an on-account payment on one party net into one figure. A book with several Currency masters is read through the INR base Tally identifies. If it has ledgers kept in another currency (foreign_currency_ledgers_excluded, each with its currency) or base-currency ledgers whose balance Tally shows in another currency (base_currency_ledgers_mixed_excluded, each set aside with all its bills), the state is partial with partial_reason currency_ledgers_excluded and partial_reasons naming the lists that are not empty: figures cover its base-currency ledgers only, under base_currency_ledgers, never a total for the whole book, and both lists are always present, paged like the bills. Each unallocated party carries `ledger_bill_wise`, `opening_balance` (the ledger's opening as of the start of the books, with Tally's sign, so a debit opening is negative, never interpreted; absent when Tally sent none, which is unknown, not zero) and a `composition`: `not_bill_wise_ledger` (the ledger keeps no bills) or `bill_wise_ledger_components_not_separated` (what is left on a bill-wise ledger after its named bills: on-account entries, an unallocated opening, notes with no reference and anything else, not told apart). `amount` is a magnitude and `direction` says which side; `unallocated.totals.by_composition` splits the gross, receivable and payable apart, by those two over every party in the requested direction before paging (a row saved without one counts under `composition_not_observed`). No unallocated figure is labelled on-account. Party detail: with `party` (a ledger name) and `detail`, the result also carries a `detail` object for that party at the same as-of. The detail's `ledger_match` names the ledger read, how (`matched`: `exact`, or `case_or_spacing`, which the answer should mention by naming the ledger read) and any `similar_ledgers` that differ from it only in case or whitespace. Passing `detail` is the request to read the company's vouchers from the start of the books (or, for a named bill that Tally's bills reports list, from the earliest date they list for it) to `as_of`; nothing is read for a party detail without it. `bill_trail` (optionally one `reference`) lists every allocation of each bill in vouchers that are neither cancelled nor optional, oldest first, with state `tied` (the signed allocations equal Tally's own balance for that bill, or zero for a bill the report no longer lists), `trail_does_not_tie` (both numbers shown) or `bill_identity_ambiguous` (more than one native row or bill date for one reference, or a native row dated differently from the allocations; nothing is merged, and the native dates are shown). Naming a `reference` starts the read at the earliest date the reports list for it, so allocations dated earlier are not read, and a reference that carries two bill dates over the whole history, and is ambiguous there, can tie when named. The detail's own `state` is `bills_listed`, or for an empty list `not_bill_wise_ledger` or `no_named_bill_for_party` (no named bill in the vouchers or in Tally's list: a ledger that keeps no bills, one that is not a party's and a party with no bills are not told apart). The vouchers and the bills reports are two reads whose extents are not compared: a voucher posted between them usually shows as `trail_does_not_tie`, but two changes that compensate, or allocations that net to zero, can still read `tied`. `unadjusted` lists the party's on-account, advance and pending note allocations and compares their on-account sum with the party's unallocated amount: `tied` means the two figures are equal, not that the composition is proven (components that net to zero are not seen); `residual_not_explained_by_vouchers` gives the difference and whether it equals the ledger's opening balance; `no_residual_row_for_party` (with `residual` null) means Tally lists no unallocated amount for the ledger (a zero residual, a ledger that is not a party's and a name that matched no row are not told apart), so nothing is tied; `not_bill_wise_ledger` lists no rows. Its rows are `row_amounts: as_allocated`: each amount is the allocation as made, never net of what later allocations adjusted against its reference, so an advance shows what was received, not what is left; what is still open on a reference is Tally's own `native_balance` beside the row, null when the reports do not list the reference or list it more than once (so no balance is chosen), told apart only by `native_rows`. Either detail is `window_returned_no_vouchers`, with nothing tied or listed, when the voucher read returned no voucher (that read is not corroborated). Cost and limits: the detail keeps the party's entries from the whole company's vouchers, so its cost is that of a `vouchers` read over the same span, which is unmeasured on a large book, and any refusal of that read fails the whole `outstandings` call. One foreign-currency composite voucher anywhere in the window fails it (`voucher_amount_invalid`, or `bill_allocation_amount_invalid` on an allocation). At most 128 data requests are sent (each sent twice, as every read is, with its census and the company marks besides), each holding at most 42 vouchers before anything is measured, so a window of more than 5,376 of the company's vouchers is always refused, and a smaller one may be. The refusals are `trail_window_too_large` (name a `reference` that `open_bills` lists for the party, and the read starts at that bill's date), `named_bill_window_too_large` (a reference was named already, so nothing narrows it further) and `unadjusted_window_too_large` (nothing narrows it, so it is not available for that party on that book), each with `reads.needed_at_least` against `reads.allowed`; a refusal comes before any data request when the count shows it, otherwise when a measured part does, with `window` listing any part already read. The detail needs a complete read (`detail_requires_a_complete_read`, with the read's own `partial_reason`) and refuses rather than cuts an answer of over 500 allocations: `trail_too_large` (name a `reference`) or `unadjusted_detail_too_large` (nothing narrows it). The limit counts allocations, not bills, so a party with very many opening bills can meet `agent_response_too_large` instead. For a ledger's master record (its group, opening balance and, with fields=compliance, GSTIN and party details), use ledger_masters instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

ageing_basis.description: Which date each open bill is aged from: due_date (the default) or bill_date. A bill whose date is after as_of has no age yet.

as_of.description: Optional: the day the open bills are read as of (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD). Left out, this computer's date, and the date used is returned as result.as_of.

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

detail.description: Optional, with party: bill_trail (each bill's allocations) or unadjusted (the party's on-account, advance and pending note allocations). It reads the company's vouchers; the description gives its cost and limits.

direction.description: receivable, payable or both (the default). Direction follows the sign of each bill's balance, not the type of party.

limit.description: The most rows to return on this page. The default and the maximum are this server's row limit (500 unless it is configured otherwise).

offset.description: How many rows to skip before this page: 0, the default, is the first page.

party.description: Optional, for detail: a party ledger's name, spelled as in the book or differing only in ASCII case and spaces. A ledger whose own name differs in case or symbols from the spelling its vouchers carry is reached by either; `ledger_match` shows its own name and, when different, `ledger_row_spelling`, the spelling its vouchers carry. The bills are matched on the voucher spelling; what Tally's outstandings reports call such a ledger is not measured, so a detail that finds no bill for a party that has some is not proof it has none.

reference.description: Optional, with detail=bill_trail: one bill reference as open_bills lists it; the read then starts at the earliest date the reports list for that bill.

top.description: How many parties to rank by gross exposure (default 25). It ranks parties only; page the bills with offset and limit.

tools.description: Return the Profit and Loss for a date range, derived from Tally's native Trial Balance: one line per reserved P&L primary group (Sales Accounts, Direct Incomes, Purchase Accounts, Direct Expenses, Indirect Incomes, Indirect Expenses), each the window's signed debit plus credit movement (a debit negative), with `gross_result` and `net_result` (a profit positive). The top-level `lines` is null while `net_result` is not established, so a derived line is never shown as the statement. Reads the Trial Balance, the group tree, Tally's own Balance Sheet and its Profit and Loss inside one company, mode and book-extent bracket; requires one INR currency master and supported date boundaries. Each line's `amount` has `sum` (of the amounts Tally returned), `present_count` and `empty_count`. tools.description: Tie the bank ledger in Tally to the bank statement already parsed by parse_bank_statement, at the start and at the end of the statement's own dates, or of the whole calendar months it was parsed for. Read-only: it writes nothing to Tally and never posts. Its check of the import journal takes the shared import-admission lock for a moment, so a build or post at the same time can be refused as lock-busy, and it can be refused by theirs; call again. It reads the proposals file named by proposals_id and proposals_sha256 (as build_import_xml does) and the book's ledger list three times: at the window's first date, at the day after its last date, and at the first date again, which catches a change dated before the window or an edit to the ledger itself (its opening balance, name or removal) made during the read (a voucher dated inside the window and posted during the read moves only the end figure and is not caught). No ledger is read when the file alone answers (window_not_recorded, window_narrower_than_statement, window_not_whole_calendar_months, window_beyond_statement_rows) or the window starts before the company's books begin (window_precedes_books_from). It reads no vouchers, and each ledger-list read has the same deadline and size limits as ledger_movement's. The proposals file is not bound to a company: pass the company_guid of the company the statement belongs to, because a different company that has a ledger of the same name is read just as readily. The window is the whole statement, from its first to its last row date, at the balances you supplied. A file parsed with from or to that left rows out is compared over those dates only if they are whole calendar months (from the 1st to a month's last day) within the statement's rows; the opening and closing are then worked out from the statement's own rows, so a gap together with the book's figure gives the statement's balance at the month edge. Any other window is not_established: window_not_whole_calendar_months, or window_beyond_statement_rows when a month starts before the statement's first row or ends after its last. So is a narrowed file written before parse_bank_statement recorded a window's balances (window_narrower_than_statement), and one written before it recorded the statement's dates (window_not_recorded); parse the statement again. The result carries the stage, the two dates, rows_without_voucher, three figures, a fixed reading and the company block. opening_gap is the book at the start of the window's first date less the statement's balance then; closing_gap is the book at the end of its last date less the statement's balance then, where stage before_build adds what this file's vouchers would put into the bank ledger (where the book would stand once the file is imported) and stage after_post is the book as it stands now; change_in_window is closing_gap less opening_gap. All three are in the statement's sign: positive means the book shows more money in the bank than the statement does. The book's own balances are not returned, but a gap plus the statement's balance at that date (for the whole statement, the balance you supplied) gives the book's balance, so they are derivable from the result. For whole calendar months the reverse also holds: the book's figure less a gap gives the statement's balance at the month edge, and change_in_window with the book's movement gives the statement's net over those months. These are totals per calendar month, never a part of a month except the part-months at the statement's own start and end, whose net a month edge's balance gives together with the opening and closing you supplied; but a month in which every other row's amount is already known (one row alone, or one row beside open cash lines, whose amounts parse_bank_statement returns) gives that row's amount. Each figure has a state: tied (exactly zero), differs, or not_established with a reason (window_not_recorded, window_narrower_than_statement, window_not_whole_calendar_months, window_beyond_statement_rows, window_precedes_books_from, bank_ledger_not_in_book, book_changed_during_read; for before_build also rows_without_voucher, when some rows of the statement have no voucher in the file because a cash line is unanswered or a row is skipped, and file_already_partly_posted, when the import journal already holds a row of this file, either of which leaves closing_gap and change_in_window not established). A gap does not say why: uncleared cheques and deposits in transit, a missing entry, a repeated entry and the wrong bank ledger look alike here, and the reading says so and prescribes no remedy. It checks the bank ledger only; a wrong party or expense ledger is not caught. Use it after parse_bank_statement and before build_import_xml with stage before_build, and again with stage after_post after a post or an import by hand. Requires one observed INR currency master, as ledger_movement does. Not yet proved against a live book. tools.description: Return the stock summary: the closing stock value per stock item as of a date, with the total of those values checked against Tally's own Stock Summary, and whether inventory is integrated with the accounts. The top-level `state` is one of three. `value_total_matched`: the items are returned, and their closing values add up to the sum of the top-level lines of Tally's own Stock Summary; only that total was compared, so `value_total_matched` can stand beside `partial` true when some items have no closing value. `no_stock_items`: Tally's own stock item count is 0, the item list is empty and the Stock Summary is empty; `items` is an empty list. `not_established`: no item is returned (`items` is null), `reason` says why and `remediation` says what to do next: `tally_stock_summary_differs` (the report has a total the items do not add up to), `tally_stock_summary_shows_no_value` (the items carry a value and the report has no amount; an empty report is not told apart from one Tally did not render) or `stock_values_not_comparable` (nothing could be compared). Such a result carries `unchecked_comparison` in place of `tie_out`, for investigation only: neither side is a stock value or a total, the items' side adds only the closing values present, and the closing-value total of a matched read is the only thing this tool checks. A `not_established` result is not held for paging, and it replaces any earlier read of the same date. A closing quantity is returned only where Tally's own plain Stock Summary shows the same item by name with the same quantity, unit and amount (`closing.quantity.state` `agreed`, with `amount` and `unit`); every other item says why not (`none_sent`, `unread`, `inside_stock_group`, `report_has_no_line`, `report_name_not_unique`, `report_differs`). In the captures the report listed only what sits directly under the root, so an item inside a stock group is taken to have no line and no quantity is returned for it (`inside_stock_group`); `totals.closing_quantity_unread_count` counts quantities that could not be read (a compound unit, or a unit with a space), which do not refuse the read. `checks` says per field what is `checked`, `checked_per_item` or `not_checked`: the closing-value total is checked; the closing quantity is checked item by item; each value on its own, the names, parents and base units, and whether the date was honoured are not. `as_of` (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD) must be a 31 March, not before the book's start or after today. The only period measured is the period ending 31 March 2026; other years' 31 March are admitted but unmeasured, and any other date is refused as `stock_summary_as_of_not_measured` before any request. The period runs from 1 April (or the book's start, if later) to `as_of`. Each item carries `name`, `guid`, `parent`, `base_unit` and `closing`; `closing` holds `value` exactly as Tally sends it, and `quantity` (a `state`, with `amount` and `unit` when it is `agreed`). Empty is not zero: an empty closing value is returned as null and counted in `totals.empty_closing_value_count`, and a value sent as 0.00 is a value. Signs are kept, as in the trial balance: a negative value is a debit, which is stock held, and Tally's own Stock Summary screen shows it as a positive value (measured on one synthetic company, licensed TallyPrime 7.1 Silver). `value_sum` adds the values with their signs, so stock held gives a negative sum, and `totals.value_sum_signs` is always `as_sent_negative_is_debit`; `value_sum` is written at the scale of the values it adds, and is null with `partial` true whenever any item's closing value is empty. The opening quantity and value are read but not returned, because their as-at date is unmeasured. `inventory` reports `integrated`, `inventory_on` and `batchwise` as yes, no or unknown (unknown does not refuse), and `basis` states what Tally reported (`ISINTEGRATED`); how the books use these values (as closing stock, or against a Stock-in-Hand ledger) is not measured. An item valued at zero or with no value adds nothing to either total, so only Tally's own stock item count vouches for it; that count followed the one delete measured (one synthetic company, one sample), which is not proof of a complete list (`checks.item_list_complete` is `not_checked`). `item_count_cross_check` reports `rows`, `tally_count` and `status`: items are returned only when the two are equal. Otherwise the read is refused as `stock_summary_item_count_differs` (both numbers under `counts`); a count Tally did not give refuses as `stock_summary_read_failed` with cause `stock_item_count_unavailable`, and a Stock Summary this Tally does not recognise with cause `stock_report_unknown`. `items` (1 to 50 GUIDs, each once) filters what is returned from the held read; a GUID not found is listed under `items_not_found`, not refused, and `totals`, `tie_out` and `item_count_cross_check` still cover the whole book. The inventory flags, the stock items and the Stock Summary are each read twice inside one company, mode and book-extent bracket, or the read is refused. Only the posted_verified vouchers are paged, as `items` from `offset` out of `verified_total`; when the response cap shortens them it sets `truncated` and `next_offset`. To read further pages, call again with `proof_sha256` set to the returned `proof.sha256` and `offset` set to `next_offset`: those pages come from the persisted proof and never read Tally again. The call is refused with `verification_proof_changed` if a newer verification has since become the batch's current proof, with `verification_proof_altered` if the saved proof no longer matches its recorded SHA-256, and with `verification_too_large_to_report` if the parts never cut do not fit the response cap. tools.description: Answer which of 1–500 proposed vouchers are already in the book. `presence` is present, possibly_present or absent, and only `present` names a book voucher. A nonempty window is read as `complete` only when its rows were checked voucher for voucher against a count ComplyEaze Bridge made of the window first, as `vouchers` labels it; ComplyEaze Bridge makes that count for every book that has held a voucher, however few, so a small book can read `complete` too. A nonempty window not counted is `partial` with reason `nonempty_window_unqualified`. An empty window is `complete` only when a read widened by a day on each side is also empty and the company has no vouchers (`company_has_no_vouchers`); it is otherwise `partial`, with `empty_uncorroborated` when the widened read is also empty but the company has vouchers, and `empty_window_wider_read_nonempty` when the widened read found rows on the neighbouring days, which cannot count the window. `present` and `possibly_present` never need a complete window and are produced either way, but `absent` means absent from the *whole* window and is only ever produced from one proven complete — a proposal that would otherwise be absent from a merely `partial` window instead comes back `possibly_present` with reason `window_not_proven_complete`. The conditional decision basis can use a voucher number on a voucher type you declare `manual` — unique on both sides, within an observed voucher type, and never onto a cancelled or optional voucher; or, for a voucher ComplyEaze Bridge wrote into a file a person imported by hand, the narration marker derived from the supplied `batch_id` and `bridge_txn_id` together. A native post (`post_import`) writes no marker, so this tool cannot identify its vouchers: one edited or re-dated in Tally can read `absent` here. Check a natively posted batch with verify_import, which finds its vouchers by the GUIDs its post created once its binding is made, before posting any of them again. It neither accepts nor reads client remote identifiers. Supplying only one narration identity component is an error. The marker reaches only the current writer identity scheme; older-scheme ComplyEaze Bridge writes stay unidentified rather than matched. Date, party and amount only ever produce candidates, with the rule that surfaced each and no ranking or score. A type declared `manual` is checked against the book's own numbering before the window is read (the company's master mark and the voucher-type numbering, 20 more requests): the call is refused, naming the types, when the book does not number a declared-manual type Manual with exactly one series that prevents duplicate numbers, when the book holds no type of that exact name, or when the numbering cannot be read (Education mode included); otherwise the result carries what the book said as `numbering_read`, or only its counts (`types_omitted`) when the rows would not fit a share of the response budget. Every type declared manual is checked, whether or not a proposal names it. The check reads the book's numbering as it is now and holds for the moment of the read: it does not know how existing vouchers were numbered when they were entered, and a voucher type saved after the read is not seen. A call that declares no type manual reads no numbering and says so. Every voucher type a proposal names needs a declared numbering method; under `automatic` Tally discards the supplied number, so nothing can be decided from it. `absent` means absent from this window, so cover the dates the book could hold. A proposal comes back `absent` only when the window is proven complete, nothing in it resembles the proposal, a voucher type declared `manual` carries its voucher number, and the party was supplied and could be compared completely; a proposal with no party (a Journal has none), no manual number, or a party whose comparison was cut short comes back `possibly_present` with a reason such as `party_not_supplied`, `manual_number_not_supplied` or `party_not_decidable`, however complete the window is. A reported difference on a `present` voucher is a finding for a person, not a work item: correcting a voucher by Alter or Cancel silently creates a duplicate instead (§9.7), and no ComplyEaze Bridge path can correct a voucher it did not write. This never dispatches import XML to Tally. To list the vouchers of a date window, use vouchers instead. tools.description: Return literal-window voucher evidence with curated metadata and redaction. Reads the full source window before selectors and output pagination; limit does not reduce Tally work. A `complete` window is held in memory for its later pages: a page after the first (`offset` above 0) is served from that read, with one marks read instead of the whole window, while the company's two marks (vouchers and masters) are unchanged, and its result carries `snapshot` (`id`, `master_alter_id`, `voucher_alter_id`, `read_at`, `reused`). `listing_snapshot_changed` has cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`; without `snapshot_id`, a later page whose window is no longer held or whose book moved reads the window again, and rows can shift between pages. A `partial` window is not held. A later page is served only for the same question: the same dates (a date is the same however it is written), the same voucher-type selector, search and grouping, and the `ledger` argument exactly as typed on the first page (a differently spelled `ledger` is a different question and reads the whole window again). Without `snapshot_id`, a page whose held window found the book moved reads afresh and carries `earlier_snapshot` (`offsets_do_not_continue` true): start again from offset 0. Only a page whose `snapshot.reused` is true continues the earlier pages: a later page with `reused` false or no `snapshot` is a fresh read whose offsets may not continue them. A change that moves neither mark is not seen; not established: whether a company feature or configuration change that alters export content moves a mark, whether a restored copy of the company with the same marks is told apart, and whether a remote writer's save shows in the marks at once. So a held page can be up to ten minutes old after its read finished; a first page is always read fresh. Use narrow dates; dense windows are unqualified and can fail source limits. `state` is `complete` only when the window's rows were checked voucher for voucher against a count ComplyEaze Bridge made of the window first, or the window was empty, a read widened by a day on each side was also empty, and the company has no vouchers (`reason` `company_has_no_vouchers`); otherwise it is `partial`, with `reason` `nonempty_window_unqualified` when rows were not counted, `empty_uncorroborated` when an empty window's widened read is also empty but the company has vouchers, and `empty_window_wider_read_nonempty` when the widened read found rows on the neighbouring days (the window's own read found nothing and those rows cannot count it, so an empty window beside a busy day cannot reach `complete` today). ComplyEaze Bridge makes that count for every book that has held a voucher, however few, so `nonempty_window_unqualified` is expected only when the company's mark reads zero while the window holds rows. Selectors and the search apply after the window is labelled, so a zero from a `complete` window is a checked zero. A voucher created, altered or deleted between the count and the read refuses with `voucher_window_part_not_admitted`, cause `part_census_mismatch`; call again. Each item carries `cancelled` and `optional` (always booleans; a source that omits or cannot assert either fails the whole read rather than guess). `post_dated` behaves differently: Tally asserts it on every voucher when the fetch list asks for it, and the key is left out only when a source does not report it (one old capture did, taken before the tag was asked for), so it is boolean only when Tally asserted Yes/No and is absent from the item when Tally did not report it. Absent is not evidence of `false` — it means ‘Tally did not say’, not ‘Tally said no’, and a caller must branch on key presence, not on falsiness, before treating a voucher as not post-dated. Neither this tool's listing nor `voucher_presence` filters out post-dated (or optional/cancelled) vouchers; the caller decides what a non-posting or unobserved status means for its own computation. (A `summarise_by` call is the exception: it sets aside cancelled, optional and entry-less vouchers and counts them, and sums post-dated ones with a count.) `reference`, `is_invoice` and `party_gstin` follow the same absent-means-not-observed convention as `post_dated`: each key is present only when Tally reported a non-empty value for it, and its absence must not be read as false or as an empty string. `is_invoice` is a boolean exactly like `post_dated`; `reference` and `party_gstin` are non-empty strings when present. A captured book with no GSTIN recorded against a party's ledger has shown `party_gstin` absent on every voucher for that party, which is not evidence Tally cannot report one. Of the voucher-type selectors (at most one of `voucher_class`, `voucher_type_guid` and `voucher_type`), `voucher_class` matches by Tally's own class functions and `voucher_type` ignores ASCII case as Tally does. Voucher-type names are editable in Tally, so a display name that is a class name, or the reserved name of any type in scope, is refused as `voucher_type_ambiguous` whenever the types of that name are not exactly the types of that class or reserving that name; the types involved are listed in `candidates` (bounded to a quarter of the response budget, with `candidates_total` and `candidates_truncated`). Use `voucher_class` or `voucher_type_guid` instead. That check sees only the vouchers in scope: the window read, after any `ledger` filter. A type with no voucher in scope is not seen, and when nothing is in scope nothing is ambiguous. When a `voucher_type` name selects no voucher, one more read lists the book's voucher types: a name no type carries is refused as `unknown_voucher_type`, with the name as `requested` and every type in `candidates`, nearest name first (bounded as above); a name some type carries keeps its zero. A filtered result carries `voucher_types`: the types `included` and every type `in_scope` (name, GUID, own reserved name, class and row count), and each item carries `voucher_type_guid`, `voucher_type_reserved_name` and `voucher_class` (null outside the measured classes). A row whose type Tally cannot resolve, or whose class answers contradict each other or its reserved name, refuses the whole read. A voucher whose amount Tally stored as a foreign-currency composite (`-$ 100.00 @ I₹ 86/$  = -I₹ 8600.00`) is withheld, not read: it still passes every date, ledger and type check, and is then listed in `withheld_vouchers` (GUID, date, type, number and cause `foreign_currency_amount_unparsed`, up to 100) with an exact `withheld_total`, the same on every page. `items` and `total` then exclude it, `state` is `partial` with `reason` `vouchers_withheld`, and `coverage` says so; the `voucher_types` row counts still include it, and the listing is also bounded to a quarter of the response budget. Any other amount Tally did not return as a plain decimal still refuses the whole read, as does a composite whose foreign and base amounts differ in sign while the foreign amount is not zero. `ledger_match` names the ledger read, how (`matched`: `exact`, or `case_or_spacing`, which the answer should mention by naming the ledger read) and any `similar_ledgers` that differ from it only in case or whitespace. Search: `voucher_number`, `reference`, `narration_contains` and `amount` (a plain unsigned decimal, matched against the absolute value of any ledger entry of a voucher, so it finds an invoice total and a tax line alike) keep only the vouchers that satisfy every criterion given. With a search, each item carries `matched` (which criteria held and, for an amount, the positions in `amounts` that equalled it). A blank, over-long or invalid criterion is refused (`search_criterion_empty`, `search_criterion_too_long`, `search_narration_too_short`, `search_amount_invalid`), and a narration phrase is refused as `search_narration_redacted` where narrations are withheld from the assistant. A voucher withheld for a foreign-currency amount is never dropped by an `amount` search, since its amounts cannot be compared: it stays in `withheld_vouchers` and the result stays `partial`. A held window is reused only for the same search, and only for the same listing or summary: a listing and a summary of one question hold separate windows. `voucher_types` counts are taken before the search, so with a search they do not add up to `total`. Summaries (`summarise_by`): Each bucket has `group` (a ledger name, a `YYYY-MM` month, a voucher type name or a group name), `vouchers` (an exact count, each voucher once), `debit` (zero or negative, as `ledger_movement` reports it), `credit`, `net` (debit plus credit) and `voucher_refs` (up to 5 vouchers by date, type, number and GUID; `voucher_refs_complete` says whether that is all of them; a `vouchers` listing without `summarise_by`, narrowed with the existing selectors, lists the rest). Debit and credit follow each entry's sign (a zero amount stays on the side Tally flagged it). A ledger bucket adds the entries on that ledger of the vouchers the window, selectors and search selected: with a `ledger`, type or search given, a counter-ledger's bucket holds only its entries on those vouchers, not that ledger's whole movement. A month or type bucket adds all the entries of its vouchers (debits and credits then equal in size), or only the selected ledger's entries when `ledger` is given. `entries_counted` says which: `all_entries` or `selected_ledger`. A `group` or `primary_group` bucket adds the entries of the ledgers under that group (every entry of the selected vouchers, also when `ledger` is given). A `group` bucket holds only the ledgers directly under that group, as the ledger master shows it (a ledger directly under the root is under `Primary`, with `reserved_name` null), so a predefined group whose ledgers sit in sub-groups has no bucket or a small one: its whole figure, descendants included, is in `subtree_totals` (each group on any bucket's chain with `covers`, `depth`, `vouchers`, `debit`, `credit` and `net` over everything under it, never to be added to a bucket of the same group, whose own `covers` says it holds only the ledgers directly under it, largest movement first, at most 60, with `subtree_totals_total` exact and `subtree_totals_complete`; they overlap, so they do not add up to `totals`). A `group` bucket carries `reserved_name` (empty for a group the book's user made), `chain` (every group from it up to the one under the root, nearest first, each with `name` and `reserved_name`) and `primary_group`. A `primary_group` bucket holds every ledger under the group directly under the root and is keyed by its reserved name, so a renamed predefined group stays one bucket and shows its current name in `group` (a group the book's user made there is keyed by its name). Each has `members` (the ledgers in it with their own `debit` and `credit`, largest movement first, at most 10), `members_total` (exact) and `members_complete`; a group bucket cannot be narrowed with a selector, so trace its vouchers through a member ledger with `ledger`. Group names are shown as the book has them (a group may be named after a party); member ledger names are masked when parties are masked. The groups are the book's masters read now, not the grouping in force on each voucher's date: each ledger's group chain is read before the window and again after it and must be the same, or the call refuses (`group_snapshot_drifted`, or `ledger_snapshot_drifted` if the set of ledgers changed). A ledger that the ledger list does not hold, or whose group chain cannot be walked, refuses the whole summary (`summary_group_unresolved`, with `cause` `no_parent`, `group_absent`, `group_name_repeated`, `reserved_name_missing`, `cycle`, `exhausted`, `top_group_not_under_root` or `ledger_not_in_catalogue`; `ledger` names the ledger that could not be placed, the group is not named, and `no_parent` also covers a parent group Tally returned that ComplyEaze Bridge will not carry). By construction a group summary adds 30 requests to the window read, with or without `ledger` (a paired, identity-bracketed read is 6 requests: the company's marks to size the ledger list first, then the ledger list and the group list before the window and again after it); in one live run each call took 64 requests (34 for the window and 30 for the group modes, as counted from the code); a book of thousands of ledgers was not measured: a book whose master-alteration mark is above 11,983 is refused first (`summary_group_book_too_large`; the limit is provisional and computed, not measured: 16 MiB, a size chosen here and not verified, over the compliance ledger read's estimate of 1,400 bytes a ledger, which that read measured at 1,104 (a book of 1,989 ledgers) and 1,221 (a real book of about 9,500) on its own list without balances, and this list read 1,175 bytes a ledger in one live run (51,698 bytes for a book of 44 ledgers; a small book, so the figure is not a basis to raise the limit); the mark is an upper bound on ledgers, so a smaller book may be refused, and the limit is about half of what the transport's own rule admits for the same list), a real book's group buckets may need several pages (use `offset`), and on a large book ledger totals are cheaper with `trial_balance`. Group summaries were checked once against a live TallyPrime 7.1 on one synthetic book of 67 vouchers: each bucket equalled the ledger buckets added up by the trial balance's own parent column and the call took 64 requests; a large book, a group renamed or moved while a window is read and a held later page were not run live. Each bucket has `position`, its place in the whole ordering (labels of ledgers can read alike when parties are masked, and a masked label cannot be passed back as `ledger`); to list a month bucket's rest, narrow `from` and `to` to that month. `totals` is the debit and credit the buckets add up to, `vouchers_summarised` the vouchers behind them, and `excluded_from_buckets` the cancelled, optional and entry-less vouchers left out (counted, not hidden). Post-dated vouchers are summed, not set aside: `post_dated_included` counts those Tally flagged Yes and `post_dated_flag_absent` those with no flag at all (the read asks for the flag and Tally asserts it on every voucher, so that is expected to be 0; only when it is not does a zero in the first prove nothing); a voucher type that does not post (a memorandum, a reversing journal, a sales or purchase order, a delivery or receipt note), if the book uses it and Tally exports it with ledger entries, is not told apart and is summed too: `basis` says so in the result. Checked once against a live TallyPrime 7.1 on a synthetic book of 67 vouchers (a year, 44 ledgers, a debug build of master at 4c30f3f9f): every ledger, month and voucher-type bucket equalled the sums over the listed vouchers, the 30 ledger buckets equalled `trial_balance` for the same year, each search returned what the same criterion selects from the listing, and a later page came from the held window in 10 small requests. Not covered: a memorandum, a reversing journal, a voucher withheld for a foreign-currency amount, `mask_parties`, withheld narrations, an item invoice with stock lines, paging of a summary past one page, `ledger` name resolution, another TallyPrime edition or release, Windows, a large book. Cost, from that one run: a plain read took 34 requests, about 7 s and about 6 MB from Tally; each ledger, month or voucher_type summary or search call reads the window again at the same cost, and `ledger` adds 12 requests there, four of them reads of the whole ledger list (a group summary adds 30 with or without `ledger`, below); for a month or more on a large book read ledger totals with `trial_balance` (it has no month or voucher-type grouping and no search; the same year's `trial_balance` took 34 requests and 2.5 s on that book; one day of vouchers took minutes on the largest book measured, a voucher mark of about a million). Bucket `debit`, `credit`, `net` and `totals` are plain decimals with trailing zeros dropped (`1000`, `-87900.5`); an item's `amounts` keep the two places Tally sent (`1000.00`). Withheld vouchers are not in any bucket and the result is `partial`. A voucher whose entries do not balance refuses the whole summary (`voucher_entries_unbalanced`). Buckets are ordered by the larger movement first (ledger, type, group, primary_group), ties in movement keeping the order in which the bucket was first counted in the window, or by month. A held window serves a later page of buckets as it serves a later page of vouchers. Each ledger entry's `bill_allocations` carries `reference`, `bill_type` and `amount`; where Tally sends them it also carries `bill_date` (YYYYMMDD, the original bill's date for an Agst Ref) and `credit_period` (a `value` and a `unit` of days, weeks or months, or `unit` `unrecognised` with its `text` when the text cannot be read); an allocation Tally sent neither for has neither. An entry's `cost_centre_allocations` lists its cost-centre rows as sent (`category`, `cost_centre`, `amount`); an entry without them has no such key, but allocations on inventory entries are not read, so no key does not by itself mean none (category and cost-centre names are trimmed; the amount is as sent; both names are masked under `mask_parties`). Each category restates the entry's full amount and the rows are not checked against it, so summing rows across categories double-counts. An entry whose list cannot be read whole (a centre with no name or no amount, an amount that is not a decimal, a centre or a category named twice, an empty allocation container, an allocation list in a shape not recognised) carries `cost_centre_allocations_unreadable` with a reason and no partial list, the rest of the response unchanged. To ask whether vouchers you mean to post are already in the book, use voucher_presence instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

amount.description: Optional: an unsigned decimal such as 1180.50; only vouchers with a ledger entry of exactly this amount (debit or credit). Each item says which entries matched.

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

from.description: The first day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

ledger.description: Optional: only vouchers with an entry on this ledger, spelled as in the book or differing only in ASCII case and spaces. A ledger whose own name differs in case or symbols from the spelling its vouchers carry is reached by either; `ledger_match` shows its own name and, when different, `ledger_row_spelling`, the spelling its vouchers carry.

limit.description: The most rows to return on this page. The default and the maximum are this server's row limit (500 unless it is configured otherwise).

narration_contains.description: Optional: only vouchers whose narration contains this phrase (at least 3 characters), ignoring letter case, accent composition and runs of spaces. Refused where narrations are withheld from the assistant.

offset.description: How many rows to skip before this page: 0, the default, is the first page.

reference.description: Optional: only vouchers whose reference is exactly this, ignoring ASCII case and surrounding spaces. A voucher with no reference never matches.

snapshot_id.description: Optional, on a later page only: the first page's snapshot_id, so the call is refused (listing_snapshot_changed) rather than continuing from a different read.

summarise_by.description: Optional: ledger, month, voucher_type, group or primary_group. The result then holds buckets of debit, credit and voucher counts instead of the vouchers, over the same window, selectors and search; offset and limit page the buckets. group and primary_group sum each ledger under its group as the book has it now (see the description).

suspense_tagged.description: Optional, true only, and only together with `ledger` (the suspense ledger): keep the vouchers on that ledger whose narration ends in a suspense tag ComplyEaze Bridge writes ("Bridge: purpose not confirmed; reclassify", or "UNIDENTIFIED - reallocate from" followed by the name of one of the voucher's own ledgers), allowing one trailing [BRIDGE:...] marker after it. Each item says which tag in `matched.suspense_tag`. This classifies by the narration text: it does not prove ComplyEaze Bridge wrote the voucher (the same text typed by hand matches), and a voucher on the ledger whose narration was edited after the tag is NOT listed, so also read the ledger without this filter and treat every voucher left over as still in suspense. Refused without `ledger` (search_suspense_tagged_needs_ledger) and where narrations are withheld from the assistant (search_narration_redacted).

to.description: The last day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

voucher_class.description: Optional, at most one of voucher_class, voucher_type_guid and voucher_type: a reserved class, matched however the book has renamed its types, child types included.

voucher_number.description: Optional: only vouchers with exactly this voucher number, ignoring ASCII case and surrounding spaces. Numbers repeat across voucher types, so more than one voucher can match.

voucher_type.description: Optional, at most one of the three: one voucher type's display name, matched ignoring ASCII case. A name that could mean more than one class or type is refused (voucher_type_ambiguous).

voucher_type_guid.description: Optional, at most one of the three: exactly one voucher type, by its GUID. Another company's GUID is refused (voucher_type_guid_foreign).
